## 1. Purpose

This procedure describes the microwave-assisted acid digestion of soil,
sediment, and sludge samples for trace metal analysis, following US EPA
Method 3051A [@epa3051a]. The digested extract can be analyzed by flame
atomic absorption spectrometry (FAAS), inductively coupled plasma mass
spectrometry (ICP-MS), or other suitable methods. This is a
near-total-dissolution method; silicates and some refractory oxides
(SiO~2~, TiO~2~) may not fully dissolve but environmentally available
metals are recovered.

For non-microwave hot-plate acid digestion, see *SOP-L65*.


## 2. Scope

- **Applies to:** Soils, sediments, and sludge samples requiring trace
  metal analysis (Pb, Cd, Cu, Zn, Cr, As, Ni, Fe, Mn, and others) at
  all EA Program sites, including urban soil lead surveys and
  photovoltaic panel site characterizations
- **Does not apply to:** Water samples (direct acidification or
  separate digestion per EPA 3005A); samples requiring complete
  silicate dissolution (use HF-based methods); organic tissue digestion
- **Location:** Advanced Laboratory, Seaver North (MARS 5 microwave);
  EA Program laboratory, SGM 133 (sample preparation and filtration)


## 3. Responsibilities

| Role              | Responsibility                              |
|:------------------|:--------------------------------------------|
| Lab PI            | Approve SOP, ensure training compliance     |
| Lab Manager       | Maintain MARS 5 microwave, stock reagents   |
| Trained Personnel | Perform digestion and filtration per this SOP |
| New Students      | Complete training before independent use; must be supervised for first digestion run |


## 4. Safety and Hazards

::: {.callout-danger}
### Critical Safety Warning

This procedure uses concentrated nitric acid (HNO~3~) under high
temperature and pressure in sealed vessels. Improper handling can cause
severe acid burns, toxic fume exposure, or vessel rupture. Read the
entire procedure and the MARS 5 operator's manual before beginning.
:::

### Hazards

- **Chemical:** Concentrated HNO~3~ (15.8 M) is severely corrosive and
  produces toxic NO~x~ fumes. Optional HCl (12 M) is also severely
  corrosive. Both cause severe burns on skin and eye contact.
- **Physical:** Microwave vessels reach 175 C and develop significant
  internal pressure. Residual pressure and acid vapor remain in the
  headspace after digestion. Hot vessels can cause burns.
- **Inhalation:** NO~x~ and HCl fumes are toxic. All acid handling and
  vessel venting must occur in the fume hood.

### Required PPE

- [ ] Chemical splash goggles (not safety glasses)
- [ ] Face shield (when opening hot vessels)
- [ ] Lab coat
- [ ] Neoprene or heavy-duty acid-resistant gloves (long-cuffed)
- [ ] Closed-toed shoes

### Emergency Procedures

For acid splashes to skin or eyes, flush immediately at the eyewash
station or safety shower for at least 15 minutes. For inhalation of
fumes, move to fresh air and seek medical attention if symptoms persist.
For vessel rupture or spill, evacuate the area and notify the lab
manager. Refer to
[SOP-L02 Hazardous Materials Handling](SOP-L02-hazardous-materials-handling.qmd).

| Microwave digestion vessels with carbon fiber sleeves | Must be compatible with the MARS 5; pressure-relief mechanism required |
| Temperature and pressure sensors (if applicable) | Consult instrument supervisor |
| Fume hood                     | Required for all acid handling and vessel venting |
| Analytical balance (0.001 g)  | See [SOP-L13](SOP-L13-using-balances.qmd) |
| Centrifuge                    | Capable of 2,000--3,000 rpm; see *SOP-L25* or *SOP-L27* |
| Mortar and pestle             | For grinding dried soil                   |
| No. 10 sieve (2 mm mesh)     | For sieving ground soil                   |
| Drying oven                   | Set to 60 C; see [SOP-L16](SOP-L16-drying-ovens.qmd) |

### Consumables

| Item                          | Cat. No. / Notes                          |
|:------------------------------|:------------------------------------------|
| 50 mL graduated centrifuge tubes | For dilution and centrifugation        |
| 15 mL centrifuge tubes        | For filtered digest storage               |
| Disposable syringes (10 mL)  | Acid-resistant polypropylene               |
| Syringe filters, 0.45 um, 25 mm | Fisherbrand Cat. No. 09-719D           |
| 100 mL beakers or aluminum crinkle dishes | For drying samples            |

### Reagents

| Reagent                       | Grade / Notes                             |
|:------------------------------|:------------------------------------------|
| Nitric acid (HNO~3~), concentrated (15.8 M) | Trace Metal grade; Fisher A509P500 or equivalent |
| Hydrochloric acid (HCl), concentrated (12 M) (optional) | Trace Metal grade; for improved recovery of Al, Sb, Ba, Be, Cr, Fe, Mg, Ag, V [@epa3051a] |
| Reagent water (Type I)        | From [*SOP-L11*](SOP-L11-milli-q-water.qmd); must be interference-free at target MDLs |

::: {.callout-note}
All reagents must be Trace Metal grade or equivalent. Analyze a reagent
blank before use; the blank must read below the method detection limit
(MDL) for all target analytes.
:::


## 6. Procedure

### 6.1 Glassware and Vessel Cleaning

1. Acid-wash all vessels, centrifuge tubes, and volumetric ware per
   [SOP-L12 Glassware Cleaning](SOP-L12-glassware-cleaning.qmd),
   Section 6.3 (10% HNO~3~ acid bath)
2. Rinse with reagent water and dry in a clean environment
3. For microwave vessels, follow the manufacturer's cleaning protocol
   (CEM recommends a cleaning cycle with dilute HNO~3~ between batches)

### 6.2 Sample Preparation

1. Weigh approximately 3--5 g of soil into a clean beaker or aluminum
   dish. Avoid obviously non-soil material (large rocks, twigs, leaves).
2. Dry at 60 C overnight in the drying oven. Do not exceed 60 C;
   higher temperatures can volatilize mercury and other semi-volatile
   metals.
3. Allow to cool. Using a clean mortar and pestle, grind the dried soil
   and pass through a No. 10 sieve (2 mm).

### 6.3 Microwave Digestion

1. Weigh 0.500 g (+/- 0.001 g) of the sieved, dried soil into a clean
   microwave vessel. For oil-contaminated or high-organic samples, use
   no more than 0.250 g. Record the exact mass.
2. Working in the fume hood, add 10.0 mL (+/- 0.1 mL) of concentrated
   HNO~3~ (Trace Metal grade) to the vessel.

::: {.callout-warning}
### Vigorous Reaction

Adding acid to samples with high organic matter may cause immediate
effervescence. If a vigorous reaction occurs, leave the vessel uncapped
in the fume hood for 1--2 hours to allow pre-digestion before sealing.
:::

3. *Optional:* For improved recovery of Al, Sb, Ba, Be, Cr, Fe, Mg,
   Ag, and V, substitute 9 mL HNO~3~ + 3 mL concentrated HCl (aqua
   regia variant). Note: HCl can increase interferences with some
   ICP-MS analyses; consult the analyst.
4. Seal the vessels according to the manufacturer's instructions
5. Place each sealed vessel into a slot on the vessel rack **with a
   carbon fiber sleeve in place**

::: {.callout-danger}
### Critical

Never place a vessel into a rack slot without its carbon fiber sleeve.
The sleeve provides essential containment in the event of a vessel
failure. Operating without the sleeve risks vessel explosion.
:::

6. Secure the rack into the MARS 5 microwave
7. If applicable, connect the temperature and pressure sensors to the
   designated control vessel(s)
8. Select the pre-programmed EPA 3051A method. Verify the following
   parameters:

| Parameter                     | Specification (EPA 3051A)     |
|:------------------------------|:------------------------------|
| Ramp to 175 C                | 5.5 +/- 0.25 minutes         |
| Hold at 175 +/- 5 C          | 4.5 minutes (remainder of 10 min total) |
| Maximum pressure              | Per vessel rating; relief mechanism must activate before failure |

9. With instructor verification that all vessels are sealed and the
   rack is properly installed, close the microwave door and start the
   program
10. After the program finishes, allow the vessels to cool inside the
    microwave for at least 5 minutes, then transfer to the fume hood
    for further cooling

### 6.4 Filtration and Extract Preparation

1. Working in the fume hood, carefully uncap each vessel and vent for
   2--3 minutes to release residual acid vapor and pressure
2. Quantitatively transfer the digest into a clean 50 mL graduated
   centrifuge tube, rinsing the vessel walls with small portions of
   reagent water to ensure complete transfer
3. Dilute to the 25.0 mL mark with reagent water. Record the final
   volume. Keep all samples as close to the same volume as possible.
4. Cap and centrifuge at 2,000--3,000 rpm for 10 minutes or until the
   supernatant is clear

::: {.callout-note}
Refractory materials (SiO~2~, TiO~2~, Al~2~O~3~) may remain
undissolved and cause persistent turbidity. If the supernatant is not
clear after centrifugation, allow the sample to stand overnight before
filtering.
:::

5. Using a clean 10 mL syringe, carefully withdraw 10 mL of
   supernatant without disturbing the pellet
6. Attach a fresh 0.45 um syringe filter (Fisherbrand 09-719D) and
   filter the supernatant into a clean 15 mL centrifuge tube
7. Use a new syringe and filter for each sample
8. Cap and label the filtered extract. Store at 4 C until analysis.

### 6.5 Disposal and Cleanup

1. Collect all acid digestion waste (vessel rinses, supernatant
   residues, centrifuge pellets in acid) in a labeled acid waste carboy
   in the fume hood. EH&S pickup.
2. Rinse and clean microwave vessels per the manufacturer's protocol
3. Dispose of used syringe filters and syringes in the acid waste
   stream (they are contaminated with concentrated HNO~3~ digest)
4. Wipe down all bench surfaces with DI water
5. Remove and properly dispose of gloves; wash hands thoroughly


## 7. Quality Control and Acceptance Criteria

### 7.1 QC Requirements

- **Reagent blank:** Include one vessel containing only 10 mL HNO~3~
  (no soil) in each digestion batch. The blank must read below the MDL
  for all target analytes.
- **Laboratory control sample (LCS):** Digest a certified reference
  material (CRM) or laboratory reference soil with known metal
  concentrations in each batch. Recovery should be 75--125% of the
  certified value.
- **Matrix spike:** Spike a duplicate sample with a known concentration
  of the target analyte(s). Recovery should be 75--125%.
- **Duplicate digestions:** Process at least 10% of samples in
  duplicate. Relative percent difference (RPD) should be less than 20%.
- **Calibration verification:** After instrument analysis, verify the
  calibration with a mid-range check standard every 10 samples.

### 7.2 Calculations

**Metal concentration in soil (mg/kg dry weight):**

$$
C_{\text{soil}} = \frac{C_{\text{digest}} \times V_{\text{final}}}{M_{\text{soil}}}
$$

where $C_{\text{digest}}$ = concentration in the digest (mg/L from
ICP-MS or FAAS), $V_{\text{final}}$ = final digest volume (mL,
typically 25), and $M_{\text{soil}}$ = mass of dried soil (g).

Since the soil was dried at 60 C (not 105 C), apply a moisture
correction if reporting on a 105 C oven-dry basis:

$$
C_{\text{soil, OD}} = C_{\text{soil}} \times \frac{100 + \theta_{60}}{100 + \theta_{105}}
$$

where $\theta_{60}$ and $\theta_{105}$ are the moisture contents at
60 C and 105 C respectively (determined on a companion subsample per
[SOP-L55](SOP-L55-soil-moisture.qmd)).


## 8. Waste Disposal

| Waste Type                    | Disposal Method                          |
|:------------------------------|:-----------------------------------------|
| Acid digest waste (vessels, rinses, pellets) | Collect in acid waste carboy; EH&S hazardous waste pickup |
| Used syringe filters and syringes | Acid waste stream (contaminated with HNO~3~) |
| Centrifuge tube residues      | Acid waste carboy                        |
| Digested soil pellets         | Acid waste carboy (contain concentrated acid) |

::: {.callout-warning}
### Acid Waste

All waste from this procedure contains concentrated HNO~3~ and
dissolved metals. **Do not pour down the drain.** Collect in a labeled
polyethylene carboy for EH&S hazardous waste pickup.
:::

## 10. Training Record

Before performing microwave acid digestion independently, personnel
must:

1. Read this SOP, [SOP-L01 Laboratory Safety](SOP-L01-laboratory-safety.qmd),
   and [SOP-L02 Hazardous Materials Handling](SOP-L02-hazardous-materials-handling.qmd)
   in full
2. Review the SDS for concentrated HNO~3~ and HCl
3. Review the MARS 5 operator's manual (vessel loading, program
   selection, safety interlocks)
4. Observe a trained operator perform a complete digestion cycle
   (vessel loading through filtration)
5. Perform at least one complete digestion batch under direct
   supervision, including a blank and a CRM, with acceptable QC results
6. Be signed off by the PI or lab manager

::: {.callout-important}
First-time users must be directly supervised for their entire first
digestion run. Independent operation is permitted only after sign-off.
:::


## Appendix A: Example Calculation {.appendix}

```{r}
#| label: mars-digestion-calc
#| echo: true
#| eval: false

# Trace metal concentration from microwave digest
# EPA 3051A, analyzed by ICP-MS

C_digest_mg_L <- 0.452     # Pb concentration in filtered digest (mg/L)
V_final_mL <- 25.0         # Final volume after dilution (mL)
M_soil_g <- 0.503           # Mass of dried soil digested (g)

# Concentration in soil (mg/kg)
C_soil_mg_kg <- (C_digest_mg_L * V_final_mL) / M_soil_g

cat(sprintf("Digest concentration: %.3f mg/L Pb\n", C_digest_mg_L))
cat(sprintf("Soil mass:           %.3f g\n", M_soil_g))
cat(sprintf("Final volume:        %.1f mL\n", V_final_mL))
cat(sprintf("Soil Pb:             %.1f mg/kg\n", C_soil_mg_kg))

# Compare to screening levels
cat(sprintf("\nCalifornia DTSC residential screening level for Pb: 80 mg/kg\n"))
cat(sprintf("EPA RSL for Pb (residential): 400 mg/kg\n"))
if (C_soil_mg_kg > 400) {
  cat("WARNING: Exceeds EPA residential screening level\n")
} else if (C_soil_mg_kg > 80) {
  cat("NOTE: Exceeds CA DTSC residential screening level\n")
} else {
  cat("Below both screening levels\n")
}
```


## Appendix B: Troubleshooting {.appendix}

| Symptom                       | Probable Cause                  | Corrective Action              |
|:------------------------------|:--------------------------------|:-------------------------------|
| Vigorous reaction when acid added | High organic matter or carbonite content | Pre-digest uncapped in fume hood for 1--2 hours before sealing |
| Vessel pressure exceeds limit during run | Sample mass too large; excessive organic content | Reduce sample mass to 0.250 g; extend pre-digestion time |
| Supernatant not clear after centrifugation | Refractory oxides (SiO~2~, TiO~2~) remain undissolved | Allow to stand overnight; filter through 0.45 um; this is normal for EPA 3051A |
| Blank reads above MDL         | Contaminated acid, vessels, or water | Use fresh Trace Metal grade acid; re-clean vessels; check DI water quality |
| CRM recovery below 75%        | Incomplete digestion; sample loss during transfer | Verify temperature reached 175 C; rinse vessels quantitatively; consider HNO~3~/HCl mixture |
| CRM recovery above 125%       | Contamination; calibration error | Check blank; recalibrate instrument; re-analyze |
| High RPD between duplicates   | Soil heterogeneity; inconsistent weighing | Grind and sieve more thoroughly; weigh to 0.001 g precision |
